units.title: Backward interpolation turns growth into contraction
units.statement: Let Φ be a continuous scalar interpolation with an exact right derivative. If Φ'(u)≥rΦ(u) at every time, then reading the interpolation from s to t gives Φ(s)≤Φ(t)e^{-r(t-s)} for every s≤t.
assumptions: Φ and its supplied derivative are real-valued on the whole real line.
At every u, the right derivative within [u,∞) is exactly Φ'(u).
The lower differential inequality rΦ(u)≤Φ'(u) holds at every real u.
No sign condition on Φ or r is required.

steps.title: Reverse the inequality by negating the curve
steps.text: For g=-Φ, the lower growth bound becomes the upper differential inequality g'≤rg required by one-sided Grönwall.
steps.lean: Negate `hgrowth`; `HasDerivWithinAt.neg` supplies the exact right derivative of g.

steps.title: Apply one-sided Grönwall between the two endpoints
steps.text: The comparison theorem gives -Φ(t)≤-Φ(s)e^{r(t-s)}, equivalently Φ(s)e^{r(t-s)}≤Φ(t).

steps.title: Move the exponential to the terminal side
steps.text: Multiply by the positive inverse exponential and use e^{rΔ}e^{-rΔ}=1.
steps.lean: Use `Real.exp_nonneg`, `Real.exp_add`, and exact ring normalization of the exponents.

units.lean_statement: Lean records the interpolation, its derivative function, the rate, and both endpoint times explicitly.
units.lean_proof: The proof applies Mathlib's one-sided Grönwall theorem to the negated interpolation and then cancels the positive exponential exactly.
units.boundary: The theorem is only the scalar endpoint comparison. It does not build a Markov semigroup, identify Φ with P_s Γ(P_{t-s}f), prove its derivative formula, or derive Γ₂≥κΓ for a concrete generator.
